body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c_e\le C_e<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that \(c_e\rho_n^e\le R_n^e\le C_e\rho_n^e\) for every \(n\ge2\), where \(\rho_n^e=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\). The upper bound is attained by a total annular local-polynomial inverse-propensity estimator, and the lower bound uses two genuine full-support uniform-design Bernoulli laws with the same supplied propensity.
body.justification: The oracle benchmark isolates information loss from treatment scarcity before any cost of learning the multiplier is assessed.
body.gap: Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign treats scalar Gaussian regression, while the present result is a multivariate causal Bernoulli contrast on a corner annulus with a supplied propensity.
body.consumer: The sharp oracle rate is the denominator in the unknown-versus-supplied propensity comparison required by the main frontier.
